directions.name: Rule Observatory
directions.short: Follow the life of a rule.
directions.description: Build a pilot observatory connecting selected laws, cases, administrative rules, and organizational regulations over time. Develop measures of replication, variation, and selection, and assess their validity with relevant domain experts.
directions.method: Longitudinal corpora · Citation networks · Text reuse
directions.deliverable: A pilot corpus and a defensible set of measures.

directions.name: Rule Dynamics
directions.description: Explore how diversity, citation concentration, variation, creation, repeal, and feedback delays shape rule systems. Compare evolutionary, nonlinear, network, and agent-based models to identify possible endogenous dynamics and early transition signals.
directions.method: Evolutionary models · Network coevolution · State-space models
directions.deliverable: Preliminary tests of endogenous dynamics and transition signals.

directions.name: Theory-Based Prediction
directions.short: Ask what the past can tell us.
directions.description: Design chronological benchmarks predicting future citations, revisions, repeals, rule survival, and systemic transitions from past evidence. Define targets, time splits, and evaluation criteria, including a university regulations proof of concept.
directions.method: Time-based evaluation · Survival analysis · Preregistered forecasts
directions.deliverable: A benchmark design; prospective evaluation belongs to follow-up research.

directions.name: Rule Evolution Simulation
directions.short: Explore how AI changes the process.
directions.description: Design experiments varying AI involvement, rule production speed, human review, model diversity, citation concentration, and feedback. Specify intervention scenarios for investigating when error correction persists or errors and authority concentrate.
directions.method: Agent-based models · AI intervention scenarios · Feedback experiments
directions.deliverable: Experimental variables and scenarios for later implementation.

hypotheses.name: Partial self-evolution
hypotheses.question: Do rules have dynamics of their own?
hypotheses.text: Rule lineages, citation structures, reused language, and semantic positions may predict subsequent citation, revision, and disappearance even after considering human intentions and external conditions, indicating dynamics beyond individual institutional actors.

hypotheses.name: Critical transitions
hypotheses.question: When does a system lose its ability to recover?
hypotheses.text: Rule systems may have multiple stable states and undergo threshold transitions. Reduced diversity, concentrated citations, and delayed feedback may weaken resilience, with slower recovery, rising autocorrelation, and variability signaling transitions.

hypotheses.name: AI timescale mismatch
hypotheses.question: What happens when production outpaces scrutiny?
hypotheses.text: When AI accelerates rule production faster than institutions can scrutinize its consequences, unreviewed rules and errors may accumulate. Shared models may amplify correlated mistakes, weakening rather than strengthening institutional correction.
